finding.claim: Unauthenticated path traversal in /dl lets any remote client read arbitrary files the server process can read, outside /srv/files (CRITICAL, Validation Tier 0; downgrade to HIGH if impact is judged limited to readable files).
finding.source: Query parameter 'f' on GET /dl (files.go:12), reachable unauthenticated on all interfaces via ListenAndServe(":8082") (files.go:34).
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, response written at files.go:18.

trace.note: Server binds :8082 on all interfaces (public ingress).
/dl is routed to download with no auth middleware.
name taken from r.URL.Query().Get("f") with no validation.
filepath.Join calls Clean, which resolves '..' against /srv/files: '../../etc/passwd' becomes '/etc/passwd'.
os.ReadFile reads the resolved path, following symlinks.
w.Write returns file contents to the attacker.

finding.guards_checked: No authentication on main (files.go:31-34) or download (files.go:11-19). No filepath.Rel, prefix check, or '..' rejection after Join. No input validation on f. filepath.Base is used only in avatar (files.go:22), not download. Null-byte rejection by Go os is an error path, not a control. Symlinks not checked. No WAF or proxy defined in this repo; deployment not verifiable. Related: download has no ownership or access check, so even with traversal fixed any unauthenticated caller can read any file under /srv/files (intent unknown). PoC: curl -g "http://<host>:8082/dl?f=../../../../etc/passwd".

verdict.guard_found: none. No auth on /dl (files.go:32, no middleware). The only input handling is r.URL.Query().Get("f") (files.go:12), which is used unvalidated. filepath.Join (files.go:13) only Cleans the path and does not contain it to root. There is no filepath.Rel or prefix check, and no '..' rejection. The error at files.go:14-17 is only a not-found path. filepath.Base at files.go:22 applies to avatar, not download. The server binds all interfaces at files.go:34.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: /dl is routed without auth at files.go:32, f is taken unvalidated at files.go:12, and filepath.Join at files.go:13 resolves '../../etc/passwd' to /etc/passwd, so os.ReadFile returns it and files.go:18 writes it to the caller. Anonymous remote clients can reach this on :8082 (files.go:34), and no control in the repo blocks it. Deployment exposure is not verifiable here, and the severity (CRITICAL vs HIGH) is a judgment call, but the finding itself stands.
